questions.text: My parents have one girl. She is their {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Daughter” oznacza córkę.

questions.text: My parents have one boy. He is their {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Son” oznacza syna.

questions.text: My brother's son is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Syn brata lub siostry to „nephew”, czyli bratanek albo siostrzeniec.

questions.text: My sister's daughter is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Córka brata lub siostry to „niece”, czyli bratanica albo siostrzenica.

questions.text: My grandfather's father is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Ojciec dziadka to „great-grandfather”, czyli pradziadek.

questions.text: My grandmother's mother is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Matka babci to „great-grandmother”, czyli prababcia.

questions.text: My mother's new husband is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Nowy mąż mamy to „stepfather”, czyli ojczym.

questions.text: My father's new wife is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Nowa żona taty to „stepmother”, czyli macocha.

questions.text: My mother's new husband's son is my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Syn ojczyma to „stepbrother”, czyli przyrodni brat.

questions.text: A married man can call his female partner his {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Wife” oznacza żonę.

questions.text: We cook meals in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Posiłki przygotowujemy w kuchni, czyli w „kitchen”.

questions.text: I sleep in my {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Bedroom” oznacza sypialnię.

questions.text: You can have a shower in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Prysznic bierzemy w łazience, czyli w „bathroom”.

questions.text: Our family watches TV in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Living room” oznacza salon.

questions.text: We eat dinner together in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: „Dining room” oznacza jadalnię.

questions.text: My dad keeps the car in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Samochód trzymamy w garażu, czyli w „garage”.

questions.text: There are flowers and trees in our {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Kwiaty i drzewa rosną w ogrodzie, czyli w „garden”.

questions.text: We keep old boxes under the roof in the {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Pomieszczenie pod dachem to „attic”, czyli strych.

questions.text: Her hair forms lots of small curls. She has got {{word}} hair.
questions.explanation: Włosy tworzące loki opisujemy słowem „curly”.

questions.text: My grandfather has hair on his chin and cheeks. He has got a {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Włosy na brodzie i policzkach to „beard”, czyli broda.

questions.text: Her hair is very light and yellow. She has got {{word}} hair.
questions.explanation: Jasne, żółtawe włosy opisujemy jako „blonde hair” lub „blond hair”.

questions.text: His eyes are the colour of the sky. He has got {{word}} eyes.
questions.explanation: Oczy w kolorze nieba to „blue eyes”.

questions.text: Lucy is kind and nice to other people. She is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Miłą i życzliwą osobę opisujemy słowem „friendly”.

questions.text: The children make a lot of noise. They are {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Kogoś, kto robi dużo hałasu, opisujemy słowem „noisy”.

questions.text: Ben doesn't talk very much. He is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Cichą osobę opisujemy słowem „quiet”.

questions.text: Kate loves exercise and plays many games. She is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Osobę, która lubi sport, opisujemy słowem „sporty”.

questions.text: Anna is from Poland. She is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Osoba z Polski jest „Polish”.

questions.text: Pierre is from France. He is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Osoba z Francji jest „French”.

questions.text: Li is from China. She is {{word}}.
questions.explanation: Osoba z Chin jest „Chinese”.

questions.text: Can I {{word}} you to my sister?
questions.explanation: W zwrocie „Can I introduce you...?” czasownik „introduce” oznacza „przedstawić”.
